Remove Detected Symmetries by Reparametrization

Source: R/symmetryReduction.R
symmetryReduction.Rd

Turns the non-identifiable directions of a symmetryDetection() result into a parameter transformation that removes them. A scaling fixes one coordinate to 1. A general direction is replaced by the invariants of that direction, held by new parameters q_<k>, searched up to the degree bounds dPoly, dDarboux and dExp. The computation runs in the Python package symident.

Usage

symmetryReduction(
  object,
  fixed = NULL,
  positive = NULL,
  dPoly = 3L,
  dDarboux = 2L,
  dExp = 2L,
  separable = TRUE,
  reportZeroCompatibility = FALSE,
  alternatives = FALSE,
  timeout = Inf,
  allowOpen = FALSE,
  allowChecked = FALSE,
  check = TRUE,
  workCap = 4000L,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A symmetrydetection result from symmetryDetection().

fixed

Coordinates with known values; scalings they remove are dropped. NULL (default) uses the gauge of object.

positive

Coordinates known to be positive: TRUE (all), FALSE (none) or a character vector. NULL (default) takes the declaration of the detection in object.

dPoly

Degree bound of polynomial and rational invariants. Defaults to 3.

dDarboux

Degree bound of the Darboux polynomials. Defaults to 2.

dExp

Numerator degree bound of exponential factors; 0 skips them. Defaults to 2.

separable

Logical. Solve separable blocks by quadratures. Defaults to TRUE.

reportZeroCompatibility

Logical. Report which coordinates each block can drive to 0. Defaults to FALSE.

alternatives

Logical. Also return the charts of the other valid pins in $alternatives. Defaults to FALSE.

timeout

Time limit in seconds for the section search of one block; a block not solved in time keeps the invariants ("invariant_only"). Unlike workCap, it depends on the load of the machine. Defaults to Inf.

allowOpen

Logical. Reduce the directions with a closed form and leave those of level "open" in place; otherwise such a direction is an error. A direction of level "verified" or "checked", and a section claim left unproven, give a warning. Defaults to FALSE.

allowChecked

Logical. Reduce also on a direction of level "checked", which holds at random points but has no proof, and on a result whose saturation check failed; otherwise either is an error. Defaults to FALSE.

check

Logical. Run the detection again on the model with the trafo applied and record in checks$loop whether exactly the remaining directions are left. Defaults to TRUE; large models may turn it off.

workCap

Number of candidate sections the search of one block may try; reaching it is an entry in limits. Defaults to 4000.

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class symmetryreduction:

blocks

one entry per set of coupled directions, with invariants, section, newParameters (the invariant each q_<k> holds), solvedDomain, coverage and status ("fixed", "reduced", "invariant_only" or "unresolved"), level, generatorLevel (the lowest level of the directions in the block), unproven (the claims of the section that are not proven) and, for a curved block, count ("exact" or "upper bound"), injective and reach. A section on a face (face) holds faceWhy, why the model is not shown continuous up to the face (NULL when it is), and faceLevel, "checked" when the resting state under equilibrate is checked at random points only.

level

how far the reduction is established, the lowest over the reduced blocks: "exact", "verified" or "checked" (a direction rests on a closed form verified with an error bound, or checked without one, or a face on a checked resting state) or "open" (a claim of a section is not proven, named under unproven).

assumptions

what the reduction assumes: domain (the declared positive coordinates) and starts (the sides of switches declared at the start), with errorBound, the probability that a verified closed form is wrong.

limits

the work budgets and time limits that stopped a section or invariant search.

checks

pins and invariants, whether every pin holds under the trafo and every invariant of a block maps to the matching new parameter over Q, failed, and with check = TRUE loop: the directions the reduced model has, the number expected, rank, dim and rankStatus, and ok.

zeroCompatibility

with reportZeroCompatibility = TRUE, the sets of coordinates that can vanish together and the condition for it.

trafo

an eqnvec over all coordinates for P() or symmetryDetection(trafo = ); NULL if nothing was reduced.

family

the valid gauges of each reduced block.

removed, remaining

labels of the directions.

dependent

labels of directions that depend on the others and need no reduction.

partial

labels of removed directions whose chart covers only part of the positive orthant.

alternatives

the other charts, each with trafo, removed, remaining, rational and pins.

discrete

with discrete symmetries in object (see discreteSymmetries()): the symmetries that can map a point of the domain into it, the fundamentalDomain, inequalities that keep one point of each of their orbits, and the coordinates they are stated in, the reduced model's for a model with directions.

coordinates, fixed, settings, call

provenance.

print() shows the verdict, the trafo, the new parameters and the sections, summary() also one line per block. Both take width, summary() also verbose and detailed, which explains each section.

Details

A chart is returned only if it is valid on the domain declared by positive. A q_<k> that takes both signs is marked [real-valued] and is estimated on a linear scale; a chart valid only for positive values of the q_<k> has coverage = "partial". print() lists the invariant behind each q_<k>.

See also

symmetryDetection(), P()

Examples

f <- eqnvec(m = "ktx - dm*m", p = "ktl*m - dp*p")
g <- eqnvec(y = "p")
res <- symmetryDetection(f, g, reconstruct = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
red <- symmetryReduction(res)
red
#> Reduced 1 of 1 direction.
#> 
#> Trafo (non-identity entries)
#>   ktl = 1
#> 
#> Sections:
#>   {X₁}  ktl = 1
#>   summary(x, detailed = TRUE) explains each section.
#> 
#> Discrete symmetries: 0
red$trafo
#> Idx Inner <- Outer
#>   1    dm <- dm
#>   2    dp <- dp
#>   3   ktl <- 1
#>   4   ktx <- ktx
#>   5     m <- m
#>   6     p <- p
symmetryDetection(f, g, trafo = red$trafo, verbose = FALSE)$identifiable
#> [1] TRUE
